withQa: Run a whole browser task in the built-in browser through a dedicated browsing subagent, and get its final answer. The subagent does NOT see this chat: `goal` must carry the whole task with every constraint, every name and date, and what to report back (for example the prices, the names, the final URL). If the user wants a picture (screenshot) of the page on the canvas, say so in `goal`: the subagent then calls browse_screenshot with placeOnCanvas. If the user wants an editable copy of the page on the canvas, set `capture: true` and say in `goal` which page or part to copy. When the task names a site or a page, pass its start URL in `url`: the browser opens it before the subagent starts, which saves a step. (To continue from a checkpoint, pass only `resume`: no `url`, no `setup`.) To prepare the page first (a known state, API mocks, a check that it is the right page), pass `setup`. Returns `{ status: "done" | "error" | "aborted" | "step_limit" | "timeout" | "setup_failed", answer, steps }`, plus `captured: { nodeId, width, height, url, title }` when the page was copied onto the canvas. When `qa: true` was set, the result also carries `qa: { outcome: "passed" | "failed" | "inconclusive" | "error" | "setup_failed" | "aborted", verdict?, reason?, steps: [{ tool, args, ok, error? }], stepsDropped? }`: `qa.outcome` and `qa.reason` are the verdict of the test. The `qa` object may also carry `consoleErrors` and `failedRequests` (lists of what the page reported during the run, with `consoleErrorsDropped` and `failedRequestsDropped` counts). The `qa` object may also carry `checks` (the results of the `qa_assert` calls and of the final `checks` input). If a final check fails, a `passed` verdict becomes `failed`. It may also carry `checkpoint: { id, complete, summary, gap? }`: pass `checkpoint.id` as `resume` in a later browse_agent call to continue from where this run stopped. `complete: false` means the replay may not reproduce the page exactly; `gap` says why. `answer` is the subagent's plain-text report of what it saw; report only what it contains, and do not invent page content that `answer` does not state. `answer` may be in a different language than the chat: report it to the user in the user's language. The browser tab stays open between calls, so a follow-up (another detail on the same page, the next step) is another browse_agent call with a self-contained goal. This tool runs in the user's browser (client side) and has no server-side execute.
